  "thinking": "Round is starting and the pad is empty. A fish has a clear outline and a telltale tail, so I'll take the pad and sketch one: a single run from the nose back along the top and bottom, with a forked tail.",
  "say": "Let's do a fish! Big round body, forked tail, eye on the head. Stroke one starts at the nose and runs back along the top and bottom. I've got the pad, so give me a sec to sketch it.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 9,
  "point": [24, 10],
  "pad": "take",
  "sketch_clear": true,
  "sketch": [
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[24, 10], [22, 10]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[22, 10], [16, 6.5], [10, 6], [5, 7.5], [2, 4]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[22, 10], [16, 13.5], [10, 14], [5, 12.5], [2, 16]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[2, 4], [4.5, 10], [2, 16]]},
    {"type": "label", "x": 18, "y": 8.5, "text": "eye"}
  ],
  "do": "continue",
  "notes": "Animal: fish. Pad taken by me. Stroke 1 = nose stub from START (24,10) to (22,10). Stroke 2 = top body line to tail tip (2,4). Stroke 3 = bottom body line to tail tip (2,16). Stroke 4 = inner fork of tail. Label eye near (18,8.5). Plan: trace stroke 1 first myself, then 2 and 3 once stroke 1 is down; ask someone to trace stroke 4 (tail fork). Keep an eye on the start: it has to knock over the whole outline."
